clue.text: Printed facts and figures showing batsmen at Kent to be exceptional

indicators.note: exceptional here means out of the ordinary arrangement, telling us to rework the letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A scorecard shows the Kent batsmen performing exceptionally well.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture (Kent is an English county side) hides an anagram: 'to be exceptional' rearranges BATSMEN AT KENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A document from a lender listing transactions and balances is literally printed facts and figures.

clue.text: Opinionated person in saloon offering unwanted advice?

definitions.text: Opinionated person in saloon offering unwanted advice?

parts.words: Opinionated person in saloon offering unwanted advice?
parts.note: a saloon is a car as well as a bar; the person meant sits behind the driver and tells them how to drive

explanation.surface: A loud-mouthed drinker in a pub hands out advice nobody asked for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' suggests a bar, but in British English it is also a family car, which is where this busybody sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a passenger who criticises the driving, and by extension anyone giving unwanted instructions.

clue.text: Nook pleasant on the outside, hard inside

indicators.note: the pleasant word lies on the outside, wrapping round the other piece
the hard element sits inside, completing the container instruction

parts.note: pleasant means nice
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A cosy corner looks pleasant from outside but feels hard within.
explanation.walkthrough: H for hard is the pencil-grading abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a recess in a wall, a small corner or nook.

clue.text: Females providing counter-intelligence?

parts.note: counter-intelligence reads as spying, but here means information given across a shop counter by women who work there

explanation.surface: Women working as spies against enemy agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter-intelligence' looks like espionage; split it as shop-counter information instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Women employed to sell in shops stand behind counters advising customers.

clue.text: Specified tot to entertain wartime dictator

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to tot up is to add
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, Italy's wartime dictator

explanation.surface: A child named as hosting a notorious wartime leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child but is the verb meaning count up; Il Duce was Mussolini's title.
explanation.definitionFit: To adduce is to cite or put forward as evidence, so adduced means specified.

clue.text: English society crook's property taken by Crown

parts.note: a crook is a cheat; the 's is just the possessive

explanation.surface: A swindler belonging to English high society has his estate seized by the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Escheat is the legal reversion of land to the state or monarch when there is no heir.

clue.text: Collection of poems briefly summed up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards
briefly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: summed means added

explanation.surface: An anthology described in brief, totted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts the last D from ADDED to make ADDE, which 'up' turns around in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddas are the Old Norse collections of mythological and heroic poems.

clue.text: Flow of air gets moisture in coach beginning to dry

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a coach is a railway carriage, part of a train; to coach is also to train
dew is moisture on the ground

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Air flows through a damp railway coach as it starts to dry out.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade wind is a steady prevailing wind blowing towards the equator.

clue.text: Prudence has friends and gets to go out

indicators.note: going out, the letters break from their places and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Prudence acquires friends and gets to go out socially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prudence' looks like a woman's name, but it is the definition; 'and' just joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Being far-sighted means planning for the future, which is prudence.

clue.text: Man of class seen around Sadler's Wells area

indicators.note: the class abbreviation is seen around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class
EC1 is the London postcode district containing the Sadler's Wells theatre, with the digit 1 read as letter I

explanation.surface: A classy gentleman seen near the Sadler's Wells theatre in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Sadler's Wells is a London dance theatre in postcode EC1; the 1 serves as an I.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name stands for any man in crosswords, a common example-type definition.

clue.text: Two doctors outside university joining a graduate for TV programme

indicators.note: the doctors stand outside the university letter, around it

parts.note: DOC is one informal word for a doctor
DR is the abbreviation for doctor
MA, a Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Two medics surround a university, joined by a graduate, in a television show.
explanation.definitionFit: A docudrama is a television programme dramatising real events.

clue.text: Material produced by wise man and fool

parts.note: a seer is a wise prophet
a sucker is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: Fabric made by a sage and a jester.
explanation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a puckered cotton fabric, a type of material.

clue.text: No time for communication? Result is muddle

indicators.note: No here means without, removing the time word

parts.note: a message is a communication
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Lack of time to communicate results in confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a confused, untidy state, a muddle.

clue.text: Book reveals awkward situation with a third man stuck in home

parts.note: to be in a jam is to be in an awkward situation

indicators.note: one piece is stuck inside the other

parts.note: in means at home
Cain was the third human, after Adam and Eve

explanation.surface: A novel shows a fix where a cricketing third man gets trapped indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third man' suggests a cricket fielding position or the film; it is Cain, born after Adam and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica Inn is a novel by Daphne du Maurier, so an example of a book.

clue.text: A spy crossing moors finally about to escape

indicators.note: the spy goes across, spanning the other letters inside

parts.note: James Bond is the fictional spy

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A secret agent crosses the moors before fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to run away secretly, to escape.

clue.text: Artlessly playing violin part, interrupted by mum going crazy

indicators.note: the violin part is broken into by the other piece

parts.note: a string is part of a violin

indicators.note: crazy means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mother goes mad while someone plays a violin badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artlessly playing' is the definition, though 'violin' tempts you to look for an instrument; 'going crazy' scrambles the mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Strumming is playing a stringed instrument casually or unskilfully.

clue.text: Irritating attempt to entertain perhaps after meal

indicators.note: after puts the entertaining piece behind the meal

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal
singing is one example of an attempt to entertain

explanation.surface: After dinner, an annoying effort at entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasing as an adjective means annoying or provoking.

clue.text: People acting outside room seen in windows

indicators.note: the people acting surround the room abbreviation

parts.note: doers are people who act

explanation.surface: Actors surround a room seen through the windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormers are windows projecting from a sloping roof.

clue.text: Grass that is found under seat

indicators.note: in a down clue, found under means the second piece comes below the first

parts.note: a stool is a seat
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Grass that is found growing under a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is not a plant but slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoolie, short for stool pigeon, is slang for a police informer, a grass.

clue.text: Praise quiet work of accountant saving pounds

indicators.note: saving here means keeping within, holding the pounds inside

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
an audit is an accountant's work
L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Commendation for an accountant's discreet work that saves money.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of praise or applause.

clue.text: Lady's exactly so, somewhat' acidic?

parts.note: Pru is a lady's name; with the 's it gives PRUS
sic, Latin for thus, marks a quotation as exactly so

explanation.surface: A woman's remark, precisely so, turns rather sour.
explanation.walkthrough: SIC is printed after a quoted error to say it is exactly as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Prussic acid is hydrogen cyanide; the question mark admits this describes an acid kind rather than acidity.

clue.text: Foot the reverse of excellent? Doctor!

indicators.note: the reverse of means read backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 as I
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A foot is the opposite of first-rate, so call the doctor!
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of a short then long syllable.

clue.text: College's foremost educators offbeat, but sparkled

indicators.note: the foremost letter is the first
offbeat means unconventional, telling us to jumble the letters

explanation.surface: A college's leading teachers are eccentric but brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: To coruscate is to flash or sparkle, so coruscated means sparkled.

clue.text: Ferocious person little good in bank

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a tier is a bank, as of seats or oars
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A fierce character in a bank is of little good.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger is used figuratively for a fierce, aggressive person.

clue.text: Pole in a bit of a quarrel

definitions.meaning: a stout wooden pole, as used for a ship's mast or boom
a sparring bout or mild argument is a small piece of quarrelling

explanation.definitionFit: Spar names both a ship's pole and a minor dispute or practice bout.

clue.text: Way-out political predictions

parts.note: way-out reads as wacky, but means taken at the way out of voting stations

explanation.surface: Wild forecasts about elections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way-out' looks like eccentric; it means at the exit from voting stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveys of voters leaving polling stations are used to forecast election results.

clue.text: One's head may be lost in a potentially hot situation

indicators.note: losing the head means dropping the first letter

parts.note: single means one; the 's reads as is

explanation.surface: A person may lose their head in a tense, heated scene.
explanation.walkthrough: An INGLE is a fireside, so literally a hot situation.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a domestic fire or fireplace, a place where heat is likely.

clue.text: Send green cart around horticultural establishments

indicators.note: around means turned about, the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Dispatch a green cart round the nurseries.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden centres are shops selling plants and garden equipment.
